programme: CTNNB1-driven canonical Wnt/β-catenin transcription (targets include LEF1, MYC, CCND1, CD44, MMP7, BIRC5, KLF4, STAT3) sets the proliferation/differentiation output of a progenitor pool, with PML acting as the brake on that output (PML nuclear bodies are a documented site of β-catenin turnover/tumour suppression) and NFIA marking the neurodevelopmental arm of the same progenitor biology (adult hippocampal neurogenesis, NFIA-haploinsufficiency syndrome).
role_in_a: In Intellectual_Disability, CTNNB1 haploinsufficiency reduces canonical Wnt signalling in forebrain excitatory neurons and produces the clinically delineated CTNNB1 syndrome; NFIA loss independently impairs adult hippocampal neurogenesis and produces its own haploinsufficiency syndrome; PML is reported disrupted (via CMV IE1) in a way that perturbs neural progenitor proliferation. Read together, all three sit on the same axis of progenitor proliferation/differentiation control, hit from three different points.
role_in_b: In Ocular_Melanomas, CTNNB1 is placed by OT and by a retrieved paper showing YTHDF3 potentiates stem-like tumorigenicity, consistent with Wnt/β-catenin pathway activity driving a proliferative, progenitor-like melanocyte state; PML is reported degraded via ALKBH3-boosted histone lactylation to potentiate tumour progression, i.e. loss of the same brake seen disrupted on the ID side. NFIA has no OT signal and no retrieved literature in this disease.
shared_axis: A single progenitor-proliferation checkpoint built from CTNNB1 output and PML restraint appears to run in both loss-of-function (neurodevelopment, giving ID when Wnt signalling or PML integrity is compromised) and gain-of-function (uveal/ocular melanocyte proliferation, giving tumour growth when the PML brake on β-catenin is removed) directions depending on tissue and direction of perturbation.
reasoning: CTNNB1 and PML are each independently documented in both diseases in the retrieved material, which is unusual for this thin a record and supports a real programme rather than coincidence; but no source states the two diseases share this axis, the joint account is my synthesis, NFIA (one of the three carrying factors) has zero placement on the melanoma side, and the base is only 12 patient-group comparisons from 2 cohort pairs.
support: PMID 42534475 (CTNNB1 loss in forebrain excitatory neurons causes memory/behavioural deficits, ID); PMID 41137963 and PMID 41789168 (CTNNB1 syndrome clinical case series, ID); PMID 35110680 (YTHDF3 potentiates stem-like tumorigenicity, plausibly via β-catenin, in ocular melanoma); PMID 41655694 (CMV IE1 perturbs neural progenitor proliferation via PML, ID); PMID 38118002 (ALKBH3/lactylation degrades PML to promote ocular melanoma progression); PMID 40459218 (NFIA loss impairs adult hippocampal neurogenesis, ID); PMID 37915986 (NFIA haploinsufficiency case series, ID). Note: PMID 42498698 is listed against NFIA but its own title concerns NFIC, a paralog — excluded here as a likely mislabel rather than genuine NFIA evidence.
how_to_falsify: In a uveal melanoma cell line, restore PML function (or block its degradation) and measure nuclear β-catenin / TCF-LEF reporter activity and proliferation; if PML loss is not required for β-catenin-driven proliferation in this tissue, the shared-brake model fails. In parallel, in an NFIA-haploinsufficient or CTNNB1-haploinsufficient neural progenitor model, ChIP-seq or reporter assay for canonical Wnt target engagement — if NFIA's transcriptional programme does not intersect Wnt/β-catenin target genes, the neurodevelopmental arm is not actually coupled to the CTNNB1/PML axis and the account should be split rather than unified.
caveats: Only 12 patient-group comparisons from 2 independent cohort pairs support this pairing, and 6 factors (RORC, ZNF300, IRX2, PIN1, MUC1, FOXJ1, TET1, EWSR1, ENO1) recur just as concordantly but are left out of the programme because the record does not connect them mechanistically to CTNNB1/PML/NFIA or does not place them in both diseases — RORC in particular has perfect 12/12 recurrence but drives a wholly separate Th17/ILC3 immune programme with no documented tie to either disease, so it is excluded rather than overlooked. Tissue pairing is blood vs uvea, so any progenitor-pool argument crosses tissue context and is inferential. The 'on the record overall' note that evidence is thin for ocular melanoma and for joint involvement applies here too: NFIA's role is asserted for ID only, not demonstrated for melanoma. The CTNNB1-ocular melanoma link also includes a second, unclear paper on conjunctival melanoma that was not used as support.
